summary: Built M3-S01 (validation, design-only, owner metadata-builder) into five files: the two Case ValidationRule components the step declares (Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save and Origin_Must_Be_Known), validation-bypass-note.md, a one-type package.xml at API 62.0, and deploy-order.md. Every element name used - fullName, active, description, errorConditionFormula, errorDisplayField, errorMessage - comes from the Step 3 inventory built out of admin/validation-rules references/metadata-examples.md (the type-in-one-table field list and Example 2, the DX source-format shape), its references/gotchas.md and references/llm-anti-patterns.md Anti-Pattern 6, plus admin/custom-permissions references/metadata-examples.md for the $Permission reference form. Both formulas open with NOT($Permission.Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation) per Q56 and test emptiness with ISBLANK(TEXT(<picklist>)) per the plan's own recorded fixture, so the declared checker exited 0 with zero findings on the first pass under --strict. No repair pass was needed. check-outputs returned ok.
confidence_rationale: Step 10: four of the five HIGH conditions hold - every emitted element traces to the Step 3 inventory, the declared checker exited 0 on the first pass, check-outputs returned ok, and every declared output was written with nothing outside artefacts/M3-S01/. MEDIUM because the fifth fails: three of the seven Questions-to-Ask rows in admin/validation-rules are deferred in this plan rather than answered - the child-record row (Q54), the post-save-automation row (Q55) and the errorDisplayField-on-every-layout row (Q57) - and stand as assumptions A11, A12 and A13. A12 is the one that decides whether these rules are invariants at all, per the workflow-field-update gotcha, and it is assumed rather than proven.

process_observations.observation: The declared checker exited 0 with zero findings on the first pass under --strict, reproducing the plan's own recorded fixture output word for word: 'Scanned 2 validation rule(s) across 2 file(s); 0 finding(s) detected.'

Run at build scope, admin/custom-permissions' own checker resolves the cross-step reference this step creates: Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation shows 2 consumers granted by permission set Case_Intake_Integration, with 0 errors and 0 warnings - so both $Permission tokens point at a permission that M2-S01 really defines.

A13's premise is checkable from the artefacts without an org: Priority and Origin both appear as layout fields on both Case layouts M1-S02 wrote, so neither errorDisplayField is relying on a field that is absent from a layout.

The step's checker acceptance_tests[0].description claims the checker verifies 'every field token in every formula resolves' and 'an errorDisplayField that resolves'; check_validation_rules.py has no field inventory and does neither, so that exit code carries less than the description promises.

Two of the shapes this step depends on carry the cited skill's own UNVERIFIED markers - the .validationRule-meta.xml DX suffix and directory, and the Object.RuleName manifest member form - while the element names and semantics used inside the files are confirmed by the guide's field table; both are recorded in deploy-order.md rather than silently adopted.

Whether these two rules are database invariants cannot be settled from the artefacts: Q55 is deferred, so A12 (no automation writes Priority or Origin after save) is assumed, and a workflow field update re-saving the record would leave a committed Case in exactly the state the rules exist to prevent.

Neither cited skill documents whether a value outside the CaseOrigin standard value set can reach Origin at all, so the unrecognised-value half of Origin_Must_Be_Known may be redundant; the three values it tests are read off M1-S01's value set, so it is at least not wrong about what is allowed.

decision_record.question: Which users and integrations must be able to save a Case the rule would reject? (Q56)
decision_record.answer: The Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case intake identities, via the Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation custom permission on the Case_Intake_Integration permission set.

decision_record.question: Is a field being marked Required on the layout meant to be enforced everywhere? (Q5)
decision_record.answer: Priority and Origin are enforced at validation-rule level because both intake channels create Cases through the API, which ignores layout requiredness.
decision_record.element: the existence and scope of both rules

decision_record.question: Does the data already violate this rule today? (Q58)
decision_record.answer: No existing Cases, so the data is clean by construction; the active=false caveat applies to rules aimed at migrated Accounts or Contacts, which neither of these is.

decision_record.question: Does the formula touch an address, a person name, or a dependent picklist? (Q59)
decision_record.answer: No. Both formulas name only Priority and Origin; no compound field appears.
decision_record.element: formula field tokens; checker's COMPOUND_FIELDS list is clean

decision_record.question: Does each message fit in 255 characters and name both the problem and the fix? (Q93)
decision_record.answer: Final text written now: 218 characters each, each naming the field to set and why it matters downstream.

decision_record.question: Is the field the error should attach to on every layout for every record type in scope? (Q57, DEFERRED)
decision_record.answer: Assumed yes (A13). Verified as far as the artefacts allow: Priority and Origin are layout fields on both M1-S02 layouts. Per-profile field visibility is not readable here.

decision_record.question: Which field does the user actually edit to cause this - the one on the record, or a child record? (Q54, DEFERRED)
decision_record.answer: Assumed the Case itself (A11). Both guarded fields live on Case and are edited there, so the child-record blind spot does not apply.

decision_record.question: Is any workflow field update or automation writing this field after save? (Q55, DEFERRED)
decision_record.answer: Assumed none (A12); M4-S03's before-save flow is the assumed sole writer. Recorded as the open risk to the rules' invariance.
decision_record.element: none - recorded in deploy-order.md and validation-bypass-note.md

decision_record.question: How should the blank test be written? (plan constraint, not a skill question)
decision_record.answer: ISBLANK(TEXT(<picklist>)) rather than ISPICKVAL(<picklist>, "") alone, because the checker's REVIEW rule fires on ISPICKVAL with no ISBLANK and the step declares --strict.
